cards.name: Transform
cards.summary: A second, keyframeable copy of position, anchor, scale, skew, rotation and opacity that renders inside the effect stack, with real per-clip motion blur via its own shutter angle.
use_for: Punch-in zooms on talking-head or press-conference shots with real motion blur for reels
Whip-pan style slides of a photo or b-roll between beats in explainers
Reframe or scale a clip BEFORE Drop Shadow / Crop so the shadow follows the moved image
Fast slide-in of a news screenshot or headline card with motion blur
Punch-in zooms on a speaker or headline with motion blur in reels and news explainers
Whip-pan / slide transitions between clips with directional blur
Ken Burns moves on photos and documents in documentaries
Shake or bounce hits on beats in trailers and hype reels
Re-framing a clip after other effects in the stack (Motion always applies last)
avoid: Leaving 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle' on: the clip gets no motion blur, which defeats the main reason to use this over Motion
Scaling far above 100 on low-resolution press photos: visibly soft and pixelated
Doubling up with Motion keyframes on the same clip: the two transforms stack and become hard to reason about
Animating without unchecking 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle': no motion blur, so moves look cheap and steppy
Scaling far above 100% on 1080p sources: soft image

params.does: Where the anchor point sits, as fractions of the clip's own frame (not the sequence's)

params.name: Anchor Point
params.does: Pivot for scale and rotation
params.typical: [0.5, 0.5]; move to a face for a punch-in on it

params.name: Uniform Scale
params.does: Locks width to height so Scale Height drives both

params.name: Scale Height
params.does: Vertical scale in % (the single scale value when Uniform Scale is on)

params.name: Scale Width
params.does: Horizontal scale in % (ignored when Uniform Scale is on)

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Rotation in degrees

params.name: Use Composition’s Shutter Angle
params.does: When true, uses the sequence shutter (no blur); set false to use Shutter Angle

params.name: Shutter Angle
params.does: Motion-blur amount for animated transforms, in degrees

params.name: Skew
params.does: Slant the image (-70..70)

cards.equivalent: Transform (AE current match ADBE Geometry2; ADBE Geometry is obsolete in AE but is the live Transform in Premiere)
cards.scripting: Position/Anchor Point are [x, y] fractions of the clip's own frame (see below); scales are percent; Rotation and Skew Axis are degrees. The shutter property name contains a typographic apostrophe (U+2019): 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle' - match it exactly. Motion blur only appears while the transform is animating and only when that bool is false and Shutter Angle > 0, so the recipe below also needs static pr_props {'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle': false} (and Uniform Scale true or both scales keyframed, as given). Standard effects render before the fixed Motion/Opacity effects, so Transform placed above Drop Shadow moves the image before the shadow is drawn. Harvested default Uniform Scale is false, so set both Scale Height and Scale Width (or set Uniform Scale true). Sampling 0/1 = Bilinear/Bicubic per AE (medium confidence on the index order). Premiere's effect list holds two entries named 'Transform' (the harvest resolved both to AE.ADBE Geometry, so they are one card); applying by name gets Distort > Transform, confirmed by the Skew and Shutter Angle rows. Position and Anchor Point are fractions of the CLIP's own frame, not the sequence's: x = fraction * source width, y = fraction * source height, the anchor (source centre by default) placed at that source point, before Motion's scale. Measured 2026-10-13 ('Ken Burns pan and zoom on a still'): on a 1080x1350 still cover-fitted into a 1920x1080 sequence, [0.5, 0.4444] put the source centre at source px (539.7, 600.0), the same as After Effects' Transform Position [540, 600] in layer pixels (539.7, 599.9), and keys to [0.5, 0.5556] reached (539.8, 748.8) in both apps; a sequence-frame reading would have been (960, 480). Convert AE layer px to Premiere: [x / source width, y / source height].

verified.note: Frame is punched in and turned: a feature-match fit against the reference gives scale 1.25 and 8.0 degrees clockwise rotation with a rightward shift, exactly the demo reframe.

merged_from.name: Transform
merged_from.summary: Moves, scales, rotates, skews and fades the clip like the built-in Motion controls, but as an effect in the stack and with real motion blur via Shutter Angle. The standard tool for punch-in zooms and whip moves with blur.
use_for: Punch-in zooms on a speaker or headline with motion blur in reels and news explainers
Whip-pan / slide transitions between clips with directional blur
Ken Burns moves on photos and documents in documentaries
Shake or bounce hits on beats in trailers and hype reels
Re-framing a clip after other effects in the stack (Motion always applies last)
avoid: Animating without unchecking 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle': no motion blur, so moves look cheap and steppy
Scaling far above 100% on 1080p sources: soft image

params.does: Clip position (frame fractions)
params.typical: [0.5, 0.5]; animate x 0.5 -> 1.5 (exit right) or -0.5 -> 0.5 (enter from left) for whip slides

params.does: Vertical scale % (acts as the single Scale when Uniform Scale is on)

params.name: Scale Width
params.does: Horizontal scale % (used when Uniform Scale is off)

params.does: Use Scale Height for both axes
params.typical: true when only Scale Height is keyframed

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Rotation in degrees

params.name: Skew
params.does: Slant the image (-70..70)

params.name: Use Composition’s Shutter Angle
params.does: When on, uses the sequence shutter (no blur in Premiere); turn off to use Shutter Angle

params.name: Shutter Angle
params.does: Motion-blur amount for animated moves

merged_from.scripting: Harvested default has Uniform Scale = false, so set Scale Height and Scale Width together (or set Uniform Scale true and drive Scale Height). The shutter checkbox name contains a curly apostrophe: 'Use Composition’s Shutter Angle' (U+2019); a straight quote will not match. For motion blur set it false and Shutter Angle 180-360; blur appears only while a property is animating. Position and Anchor Point are frame fractions. Sampling 1 (Bicubic) is sharper for big scale-ups; the 0/1 label order is assumed from After Effects (Bilinear, Bicubic). Premiere's effect list holds two entries named 'Transform' (the harvest resolved both to AE.ADBE Geometry); applying by name gets this Distort > Transform, which can be confirmed by the Skew and Shutter Angle rows being present. The recipe is a 0.25 s punch-in with real motion blur.

verified.note: Frame punched in to 130%, rotated about 8 degrees and skewed, with black wedges exposed at the top-right and bottom-left corners.

cards.name: Turbulent Displace
cards.summary: Warps the image with fractal noise so it ripples, bulges or twists like heat haze, water or a waving flag; animating Evolution makes the warp move.
use_for: Flashback / memory sequences in documentaries with a gentle animated warp
Make a still flag or banner photo appear to wave in an explainer
Heat-haze over desert, road or summer rally footage
Liquid warp transition: keyframe Amount up into a cut and down after it
avoid: High Amount with low Size on faces: features smear and look grotesque
Pinning set to none: frame edges pull in and show black borders
Static Evolution: a frozen warp looks like a broken render, not motion

params.name: Displacement
params.does: Warp type dropdown (Turbulent, Bulge, Twist, smoother and directional variants)

params.name: Amount
params.does: Strength of the displacement

params.name: Size
params.does: Scale of the noise pattern (bigger = broader waves)

params.name: Complexity
params.does: Detail of the noise (more octaves)

params.name: Evolution
params.does: Noise phase in degrees; keyframe to animate

params.name: Offset (Turbulence)
params.does: Shifts the noise pattern; keyframe for drifting/flowing

params.name: Pinning
params.does: Which edges stay fixed so borders do not pull in

params.name: Cycle Evolution
params.does: Makes Evolution loop every 'Cycle (in Revolutions)' turns for seamless loops

Pinning.2: Pin All (default; label assumed from AE)

cards.scripting: Dropdown indices: Displacement range is 0..10 = AE's 9 modes plus 2 separator slots (3 and 7); 0-2 are safe, 4-6 and 8-10 follow AE's menu order (medium confidence, never set 3 or 7). Pinning range 0..16 also contains separators and its labels are not harvested: keep default 2 (Pin All per AE default), which stops the frame edges pulling in. Evolution is degrees. The batch has two rows named 'Random Seed': the number (seed) and a bool 'Random Seed#2' that is the Evolution Options group marker - set only 'Random Seed'. 'Evolution Options' is also a group header bool. 'Antialiasing for Best Quality' 0/1 = Low/High (AE order). Resize Layer does nothing useful in Premiere (clip bounds are the frame). Demo Amount 80 at Size 150 is a clearly visible wobble that keeps the frame readable; above ~120 faces smear.

verified.note: Whole frame is warped into liquid, wavy ripples (stripes, foreground blocks and figures bend like heat haze or a waving flag), matching the card.

cards.name: Twirl
cards.summary: Spins the pixels around a centre point, strongest at the centre and fading to nothing at the twirl radius, like a whirlpool.
use_for: Comic 'head spinning' moment in political satire reels
Spiral transition: keyframe Angle up on the outgoing clip and down on the incoming one
Dream or hypnosis beat in a story-driven explainer
avoid: Using it as a serious documentary transition: reads as cheap 90s video toaster
Large Angle with a small radius on faces: ugly smear around the centre

params.name: Angle
params.does: Amount of twist in degrees (sign sets direction)

params.name: Twirl Radius
params.does: Size of the twirled area as % of the frame

params.name: Twirl Center
params.does: Centre of the spiral

cards.scripting: Angle in degrees, Twirl Radius in percent (0-100), Twirl Center as frame fractions. For a twirl transition put matching keyframes on both clips around the cut and add a short Cross Dissolve.

verified.note: Frame is spun into a strong whirlpool spiral around the centre, easing off toward the corners, with black empty areas pulled in from outside the layer.

cards.name: Ultra Key
cards.summary: Premiere's main chroma keyer: picks a screen colour (usually green or blue) and makes it transparent, with matte cleanup, spill suppression and colour correction of the foreground.
use_for: Put a green-screen presenter over news graphics or b-roll for an AI-education explainer
Key stock green-screen overlays (smoke, explosions, subscribe buttons, phone mockups)
Remove a solid colour background from a supplied logo or graphic animation
Anchor-style political explainer with the host over a map or headline wall
avoid: Applying it to ordinary footage: it punches holes wherever the key colour appears (green in flags, clothing, foliage)
Leaving Key Color at the harvested default (black): it keys the wrong pixels (or nothing) until it is set to the actual screen colour
Keying low-bitrate social/WhatsApp green-screen clips with Aggressive + high Choke: blocky, chattering edges; garbage-matte and use Default first
Over-raising Choke/Soften: hair and edges turn mushy; use Spill Suppression instead of crushing the matte

params.name: Key Color
params.does: The screen colour to remove
params.typical: sample the screen, e.g. #00B140 green or #0047BB blue

params.name: Setting
params.does: Preset strength: Default, Relaxed, Aggressive, Custom

params.name: Output
params.does: Composite, Alpha Channel (matte view) or Color Channel
params.typical: 1 to check the matte, 0 for final

params.name: Transparency
params.does: How transparent the keyed area becomes

params.name: Tolerance
params.does: How far from the key colour still counts as screen

params.name: Pedestal
params.does: Removes low-level noise from the matte

params.name: Choke
params.does: Shrinks the matte edge inward

params.name: Spill
params.does: Strength of green/blue spill removal on the subject

cards.scripting: Key Color is a colour property; the harvested default decodes to black, so always set it (sample the real screen; #00B140 / #0047BB are only nominal chroma green / blue). Setting changes the Matte Generation values; editing any of those switches Setting to Custom (3), so set Setting first, then fine-tune. Rows named '' and the bools 'Matte Generation', 'Matte Cleanup', 'Spill Suppression', 'Color Correction' are group headers - do not set them. Whether setting Setting from a script re-fills the Matte Generation sliders the way the UI menu does is not verified: when it matters, also set Transparency/Highlight/Shadow/Tolerance/Pedestal explicitly. Demo keys test plate A's tan wall in Composite output (keyed areas render black on an empty track below). The test footage has a warm cast that puts skin within a few chroma steps of the wall, so the key colour is the wall nudged toward yellow (#B09A5F, not the raw wall sample #B0935E) to spare skin; even so the faces render at about half brightness (partly keyed) in the demo frame; an off-frame colour such as green keys nothing. Put the background on the track below; use a mask or Crop as a garbage matte for screen edges.

verified.note: The tan wall is keyed out to black (transparent over the empty track, 37% of the frame) in Composite output, a clear chroma cutout; the warm-cast faces and stripes come out partly transparent (about half brightness) as this footage is not a screen shot.

cards.name: Unsharp Mask
cards.summary: Sharpens by boosting contrast along edges, with a radius for how wide the edge boost is and a threshold so flat areas and noise are left alone.
use_for: Crisp up soft upscaled archival or AI-generated clips in documentaries
Sharpen press photos and screenshots used as b-roll in news reels
Restore bite after a punch-in done with the Transform effect placed above it in the stack
avoid: High Amount with large Radius: bright halos around edges and crunchy skin
Sharpening heavily compressed WhatsApp/social footage: it amplifies blocks and noise
Negative Amount as a blur substitute: use Gaussian Blur instead

params.name: Amount
params.does: Strength of the sharpening (negative softens)

params.name: Radius
params.does: Width in pixels of the edge contrast boost

params.name: Threshold
params.does: Minimum edge contrast before sharpening applies (0-1, normalised)

cards.scripting: Harvested default Amount is 0, so the effect does nothing until Amount is set. Threshold is normalised 0-1 (same as AE's current 'ADBE Unsharp Mask2'; only the legacy AE effect used 0-255 levels, so divide old values by 255). 'Color Mode' is a bool with no documented meaning in this harvest; leave it at false. Apply after scaling effects (below Transform in the stack) so the sharpening works at output resolution. The fixed Motion effect always renders AFTER every standard effect, so a punch-in done with Motion Scale enlarges the halos too; for a sharpened punch-in scale with Transform above Unsharp Mask, or sharpen on an adjustment layer.

verified.note: Edges are clearly crisper with visible halos (high-frequency energy 2.7x the reference) while the image stays intact, the sharpened look described.

cards.name: VR Chromatic Aberrations
cards.summary: Projection-aware RGB split for 360/VR footage: the red, green and blue channels are pushed apart, increasing with distance from a point of interest.
use_for: Stylised lens fringing on 360 footage for VR or YouTube 360 uploads
Lens-style edge fringing on a flat reel shot for a tech/AI channel look, with the centre (Point of Interest) kept clean
Quick RGB-split hit on a beat when keyframed
avoid: On flat 16:9 footage the effect still assumes an equirectangular frame, so fringing bends near top/bottom and wraps across the left/right edges; for flat glitch/RGB-split looks prefer Premiere 26's RGB Split effect
Large aberration on news footage: looks like a broken camera, hurts credibility

params.name: Aberration (Red)
params.does: Offset of the red channel

params.name: Aberration (Blue)
params.does: Offset of the blue channel

params.name: Aberration (Green)
params.does: Offset of the green channel

params.name: Point of Interest
params.does: Where the image stays clean; fringing grows away from it

params.name: Falloff Distance
params.does: How far from the point of interest the fringing ramps in

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: Monoscopic / stereo over-under / stereo side-by-side

cards.equivalent: VR Chromatic Aberrations (AE Immersive Video); flat-footage alternative in Premiere 26: RGB Split
cards.scripting: Mettle SkyBox effect (Immersive Video folder). The unnamed rows map to the AE version: the first '' bool (default true) is 'Auto VR Properties' and the last '' bool is 'Falloff Invert'; neither is addressable by name. While Auto VR Properties is on (the default) Frame Layout and the Field of View sliders are probably taken from the sequence's VR settings and the sliders are ignored (unverified), so do not rely on setting them. The exact unit of the Aberration values and the direction of Falloff Distance are not verified - demo values are deliberately strong (default is only -10/+10); check a frame before using subtle values.

verified.note: Strong red/green/blue fringing splits around every edge (stripes, faces, flowers), a clear RGB-split look.

cards.name: VR Color Gradients
cards.summary: Paints a soft multi-point colour gradient (up to 8 coloured points) over the frame, seamless for 360 footage, blended onto the clip with its own opacity and blending mode.
use_for: Colour wash or duotone tint over b-roll for stylised reels
Animated gradient background for title and quote cards (apply to a colour matte)
Brand-coloured tint over 360 footage without a visible seam
avoid: Leaving Opacity at 100 with the default blending mode: the gradient can cover the shot completely
Rainbow defaults (8 saturated points) on serious news footage: looks like a kids' filter

params.name: Points Number
params.does: How many of the 8 colour points are used

params.name: Color 1
params.does: Colour of point 1 (Color 2..8 likewise)

params.name: Point 1
params.does: Position of point 1 (Point 2..8 likewise)

params.name: Gradient Power
params.does: How far each point's colour spreads

params.name: Gradient Blend
params.does: Softness of the transition between points

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Mix of the gradient over the clip

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: How the gradient combines with the clip (0-21)

cards.equivalent: VR Color Gradients (AE Immersive Video); flat-footage alternative in Premiere: 4-Color Gradient
cards.scripting: Points are frame fractions; harvested defaults are a 4x2 grid at y 0.33/0.66. Default colours decode to red, cyan, green, yellow, blue, magenta, black, white for points 1-8. Blending Mode is a 0-21 dropdown whose labels are not verified (default 1, probably Normal as in AE's Fractal Noise-style menus): keep it and control strength with Opacity. Ignore unnamed rows (the first '' bool, default true, is 'Auto VR Properties'; the rest are group ends) and the 'Points' header bool. Only the first Points Number points are used. On flat footage it works as a plain gradient wash.

verified.note: Soft orange wash on the left, purple in the middle and cyan on the right blended over the photo at half opacity, as described.

cards.name: VR De-Noise
cards.summary: Projection-aware noise reduction for 360/VR footage that smooths grain and sensor noise without a visible seam at the frame edges; in this Premiere install it is also the only general-purpose video denoiser in the effect list, so it gets used on flat footage too.
use_for: Clean low-light 360 footage before grading
Reduce grain on noisy night-rally or indoor event clips before sharpening
Smooth noisy AI-upscaled clips in a documentary
avoid: High Noise Level on faces: waxy, plastic skin
Heavy settings on detailed footage (hair, fabric, small on-screen text): fine detail is smoothed away with the noise
Expecting dedicated-denoiser quality (Neat Video and similar): it is a simple strength control, so test a frame

params.name: Noise Level
params.does: Strength of noise reduction (0-1)

params.name: Noise Type
params.does: Noise model dropdown (two options, labels unverified)

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: Monoscopic / stereo over-under / stereo side-by-side

cards.equivalent: VR De-Noise (AE); for flat footage Remove Grain
cards.scripting: Only Noise Type and Noise Level do anything visible; ignore the unnamed bool (it is 'Auto VR Properties', default true, not addressable by name). Noise Type 0/1 labels are not harvested. Demo uses 0.8 so the smoothing is obvious on a clean still shot; on clean footage the change is subtle at low values. Slows playback: render previews.

verified.note: Image is visibly smoothed (fine detail down about 40% versus the reference) with slightly smeared frame edges, the clean/soft look described.

cards.name: VR Digital Glitch
cards.summary: Procedural digital glitch: colour channel corruption, blocky geometric displacement and noise, concentrated around a point of interest and seamless for 360 footage.
use_for: Glitch-hit transition on a beat in reels (keyframe Master Amplitude up and down across the cut)
'Breaking news' or 'system error' sting in political satire
Tech/AI channel intros and hacker-themed explainer moments
Glitch reveal of a logo or headline card
avoid: Leaving it on for a whole clip at full amplitude: exhausting and unreadable
Using on serious documentary footage: reads as gimmick
Forgetting to animate: with default settings it is on at full strength for the entire clip

params.name: Master Amplitude
params.does: Overall glitch strength

params.name: Color Distortion
params.does: Amount of colour channel corruption

params.name: Geometry Distortion X
params.does: Horizontal block displacement

params.name: Geometry Distortion Y
params.does: Vertical block displacement

params.name: Distortion Rate
params.does: How fast the glitch pattern changes over time

params.name: Distortion Complexity
params.does: Detail/number of glitch blocks

params.name: Noise Strength
params.does: Adds digital noise on top

params.name: POI Scale
params.does: Size of the glitched area around Point of Interest (100 appears to cover the whole frame; unverified)

cards.equivalent: VR Digital Glitch (AE Immersive Video); Premiere 26 flat-footage alternatives: RGB Split effect, or the Glitch / VHS Damage transitions on a cut
cards.scripting: Defaults already glitch hard (Master Amplitude 100, Color 50, Geometry X 50), so keyframe Master Amplitude to confine it; the demo backs everything off so the frame stays readable. For a one-shot glitch between two clips the built-in Glitch transition is simpler than keyframing this. Whether the glitch animates on its own via Distortion Rate or needs Distortion Evolution / Color Evolution keyframes is not verified - keyframing Distortion Evolution is the safe way to guarantee movement. Ignore unnamed rows (the first '' bool, default true, is 'Auto VR Properties') and header bools (Distortion, Transform, Sub Settings, Noise). Point of Interest / POI Scale / POI Aspect appear to localise the glitch; exact behaviour unverified. Translate X/Y/Z range only 0-10.

verified.note: Blocky pixel tearing, scattered displaced chunks and RGB fringing break up the subjects, a clear digital-corruption glitch.

cards.name: VR Fractal Noise
cards.summary: Generates seamless spherical fractal noise (clouds, smoke, turbulence) over the clip, with its own opacity and blending mode; Evolution animates it.
use_for: Drifting smoke or fog layer over trailer shots and title cards
Animated texture background for quote cards in documentaries (on a colour matte)
Subtle moving haze over a static press photo to add life
avoid: Opacity 100 with the default blend: the noise replaces the picture entirely
Static (un-keyframed) Evolution: looks like a frozen dirty lens

params.name: Fractal Type
params.does: Noise style dropdown (4 options, labels unverified)

params.name: Contrast
params.does: Contrast of the noise

params.name: Brightness
params.does: Brightness offset of the noise

params.name: Complexity
params.does: Detail octaves

params.name: Scale
params.does: Size of the noise features

params.name: Evolution
params.does: Animates the noise shape (degrees)

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Mix over the clip

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: How the noise combines with the clip (0-21)

cards.scripting: Premiere has no flat Fractal Noise effect, so this is the only built-in procedural cloud/smoke generator; on flat footage it works but wraps seamlessly left-right. Fractal Type 0..3 and Blending Mode 0..21 labels are not verified (Blending Mode default 1, probably Normal; keep it and use Opacity). Ignore unnamed rows (the first '' bool, default true, is 'Auto VR Properties') and header bools (Transform, Sub Settings). Tilt/Pan/Roll rotate the noise sphere (degrees) and can also be keyframed for drift. For a full-frame texture card, apply to a colour matte at Opacity 100.

verified.note: Grey smoky fractal clouds are overlaid across the whole frame at partial opacity, a moody fog/haze look.

cards.name: VR Blur
cards.summary: Projection-aware blur for 360/VR footage that blurs evenly across the sphere and across the left/right seam.
use_for: Blur 360 footage for a title or menu backdrop without a seam line
Defocused background under text in a 360 explainer
Blur-in / blur-out transitions on immersive clips
avoid: On flat 16:9 footage: left and right edges blur into each other and the top/bottom blur gets stretched; use Gaussian Blur instead
Very high Blurriness on long clips: slow to play back

params.name: Blurriness
params.does: Blur amount

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: Monoscopic / stereo over-under / stereo side-by-side

params.name: Horizontal Field of View
params.does: Horizontal coverage of the frame in degrees

cards.equivalent: VR Blur (AE); for flat footage Gaussian Blur
cards.scripting: Only Blurriness matters for normal use; ignore the unnamed bool (it is 'Auto VR Properties', default true, not addressable by name). Prefer Gaussian Blur on flat footage because of the seam wrap. Keyframe Blurriness for blur transitions.

verified.note: Entire frame is heavily and evenly blurred (detail down about 75%) so faces and stripes lose all detail.

cards.name: VR Glow
cards.summary: Adds a soft bloom around the brightest parts of the image (above a luma threshold), with radius, brightness, saturation and an optional tint; seamless for 360 footage and often used as a glow on flat footage too.
use_for: Cinematic highlight bloom on trailer shots and night rally lights
Dreamy glow for flashback or tribute segments in documentaries
Glow on bright text, logos or neon graphics in tech-channel reels
avoid: Low Luma Threshold: the whole frame washes out and loses contrast
On flat footage, glow from bright areas at one edge can wrap to the opposite edge
Strong glow on faces in news footage: looks like a beauty filter

params.name: Luma Threshold
params.does: Brightness above which pixels glow (0-1)

params.name: Glow Radius
params.does: How far the glow spreads

params.name: Glow Brightness
params.does: Intensity of the glow

params.name: Glow Saturation
params.does: Colour saturation of the glow

params.name: Tint Color
params.does: Colours the glow, but only when the 'Use Tint Color' checkbox is on (that checkbox is the unnamed bool just before it, default off, not settable by name)
params.typical: leave; tint the glow with Lumetri or use Wonder Glow for a coloured glow

cards.equivalent: VR Glow (AE Immersive Video) / Glow; Premiere 26 flat-footage alternatives: Wonder Glow, Edge Glow
cards.scripting: Unnamed rows map to the AE version: the first '' bool (default true) is 'Auto VR Properties' and the '' bool before Tint Color is 'Use Tint Color' (default false), so Tint Color (default white) has no effect unless that checkbox is turned on by hand - neither bool is addressable by name. Luma Threshold 0.9 by default means only near-white pixels glow, so a typical shot shows little until it is lowered to ~0.6-0.8; below ~0.5 with Brightness > 2 the frame washes out. Keyframe Glow Brightness for a flash/bloom hit. For flat reels Wonder Glow / Edge Glow have no seam wrap and more shaping controls.

verified.note: Bright wall areas and the lamps bloom with a warm soft glow while the darker clothing stays intact.
